note: THE SAME RULE OVER SIX MORE ESCAPES, so an implementation is not written against one character. Emacs answers (")" "{" "z" "." "|" "<"): `\\)', `\\{', `\\z', `\\.', `\\|' and `\\<' are each just the character. Note what that means for a regexp written as a string: the reader has already eaten one backslash, so `"\\|"' reaches the engine as a bare `|' -- which is why a regexp alternation is spelled with TWO backslashes in source. kg refuses each of them.
